title: Etta and the Pigeon's Button Rescue
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a town that always smelled like cinnamon and warm bread, lived Etta, a cheerful baker’s apprentice. Her nose was often dusted with flour, her heart as warm as her oven, her hands able to make amazing things from simple ingredients. Every day she arranged pastries: a swirl of sweet cream, a sprinkle of sparkling sugar, and for a special finish the most brilliant blue buttons. Not just any buttons. Her treasures, each shining like a tiny piece of summer sky.

Her best friend, Skiff, was a remarkably observant gull, feathers the colour of a stormy sea, eyes that twinkled with mischief. He watched from the bakery window, always ready for an adventure, or at least a good crumb. His squawks were a cheerful song to her ears.

Every day the bakery was a symphony that tickled the nose and made tummies rumble: vanilla, chocolate, the warm hug of bread. Skiff missed nothing. He squawked if a crumb was about to fall, flapped a blur of grey and white when she pulled golden gingerbread from the oven, and kept the flies away with a quick swoop.

Until one day a shadow flitted past the open window, quick as a wink. Zip. Zap. A bold, bossy-looking pigeon, feathers the colour of dusty pavements and an air of great importance, swooped in and snatched the biggest, bluest button right off her apron: the one she had been saving for the Queen’s magnificent Berry Tart.

Etta gasped, hands to her flour-dusted chest. Not just a button. The best part of her baking. “Skiff! My button! That cheeky pigeon took the Queen’s Berry Tart button!”

Because of that they were instantly in pursuit. Etta scrambled out, running shoes on cobblestones. Skiff launched with a mighty squawk that echoed through the market, keen eyes like tiny telescopes on the fluttering grey speck against blue sky. The chase led across colourful stalls. She dodged baskets of plump apples and towers of golden cheeses. He wove through the air. The pigeon darted as if it knew every twist of town.

Because of that the chase continued through a maze of narrow alleyways. Laundry flapped like colourful flags. The air was thick with cooking onions and drying herbs. Skiff, soaring, acted as her eyes. “He’s heading for the old clock tower!” The path led away from the busy town toward quieter forgotten corners.

Until finally the pigeon zipped into a dark dusty loft above an abandoned bookshop. Etta, puffing, followed Skiff’s insistent cries. The loft was a forgotten kingdom: cobwebs like lace, forgotten treasures piled high, sunlight through grimy windows illuminating dust motes like tiny fairies. The pigeon perched on a high beam. Next to it, a nest—not of twigs and straw, but of buttons. Hundreds of them, all shapes and sizes, sparkling like jewels. Clustered at the centre, a hoard of brilliant blue ones just like hers.

Then she realized something astonishing. The pigeon was not stealing buttons to keep. A pile of old rolled paper tied with faded ribbon, brittle and ancient. The bird, instead of squawking fiercely, cooed softly. Etta picked up a letter, ink faded but readable. The holes where the ribbon used to tie it had lost their blue buttons, leaving gaps. This pigeon was a descendant of the old carrier pigeons. Their job, long ago, was to carry messages across great distances. This diligent bird was gathering the very things that once helped secure those precious messages, to mend the pigeon post’s ancient tattered nest. Old paper. Soft coo. Forgotten threads and smooth cool buttons. A discovery far more amazing than any pastry.

Ever since then the market was safe for blue buttons. Etta always left a few extra sweet crumbs and a spare shiny blue button just outside the loft, a small thank-you. Sometimes she even left a tiny note attached, just for them.
